# Amr: tool sheets for ChatGPT

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-mascot-context-brief.mjs --tools from context-sheets.json. Edit the JSON, then run the script. -->

Fifty sheets of Amr (S65–S114), one for each of 50 tools on the website. Each gives him that tool's props and seven poses: opening the tool, and its key moments (a blocker raised and cleared, a vote revealed, a goal hit). They are drawn with **ChatGPT image generation** to [the same master block](AMR-ART-BRIEF.md#2-master-block) and [context rules](AMR-CONTEXT-BRIEF.md#context-rules) as S11–S64, plus the tool rules below, which carry the lessons of [hair rounds 2](AMR-HAIR-ROUND-2.md) and [3](AMR-HAIR-ROUND-3.md).

The site switches a tool's scenes on only once its sheet has come back, passed review and been built into a pack, so the batches can come back one at a time.

## How to run a batch

1. Start a new ChatGPT conversation. Upload one batch's zip (`AMR_Tool_Sheets_A.zip` … `AMR_Tool_Sheets_E.zip`) and paste its kickoff message (the prompt page has a copy button for each). The zip holds `AMR-TOOLS-CHATGPT.md` and the five references.
2. The references: `ref-1-stance.png` (ref-1), [`ref-current.png`](reference/ref-current.png) (him as the packs show him today), [`ref-hair-fix-3.png`](reference/ref-hair-fix-3.png) (the haircut to match, and the hair to avoid), `ref-3-range.png` (ref-3) and the corrected `S01-faces.png` (ref-4). Five is the most the image tool takes at once.
3. Settings, as before: **1536 × 1024**, **transparent background**, **PNG**, **high** quality, one image per sheet.
4. Check every sheet against [the checklist](#the-checklist). To fix one slot, ask for an edit of the same image: _"Keep every slot exactly as it is except slot N. Redraw only slot N: …"_. If more than two slots are wrong, ask for the sheet again.
5. Send each batch back as one zip, under the sheets' file names.

## The checklist

- [ ] The haircut matches S01 and ref-current: short and close to his skull, no dome on top, a thin even layer down the sides to the tops of his ears, very dark brown-black with soft highlights. No curls, and never brown.
- [ ] Smooth, soft shading on his face and shirt, like S01: no faceted, patchy or painterly shading, and no extra wrinkles.
- [ ] Only the props the sheet names, the same in every slot that uses them. No text, letters, numbers or logos (except a symbol the sheet allows).
- [ ] His clothes, lanyard, badge, the black band on his right wrist and the silver watch on his left, exactly as in ref-1.
- [ ] Transparent background, 4 × 2 slots, one figure per slot, nothing touching a slot edge. Slot 1 is the standard stance.

Claude then checks every sheet head by head against S01 (hair outline, texture and colour, shading, props) before building it, and sends a one-slot redo prompt for anything that drifted.

## The batches

**Tools, batch A: planning, and impediments.** Opened most often: sprint capacity and goals, refinement, forecasts, roadmaps, cross-team syncs and blockers. (`AMR_Tool_Sheets_A.zip`)

S65 Sprint capacity · S66 Sprint goal · S67 Refinement · S68 Walking skeleton · S69 Release forecast · S70 PI planning · S71 Epic roadmap · S72 Scrum of scrums · S73 Dependency map · S74 Impediments

**Tools, batch B: review, retro and delivery.** Sprint review, retro actions, premortem, six hats, canvas, and the delivery charts. (`AMR_Tool_Sheets_B.zip`)

## Tool rules

They come after the master block and the context rules in every prompt.

```text
TOOL SHEETS (S65 and later). Each sheet gives Amr the props of one tool on the website.
- REFERENCES IN THIS ROUND: ref-1 is his standard stance. ref-current shows him as he is today: his face, his haircut from the front, turned and looking down, and the smooth way he is rendered; use it wherever the master block says ref-hair or ref-2. ref-hair-fix-3 shows the haircut to match (TARGET) and the hair to avoid (NOT THIS). ref-3 shows poses he already has. ref-4 is the approved S01 sheet: match its face and haircut exactly.
- HAIR (this overrides any other hair description): exactly the haircut in ref-4 and in the TARGET row of ref-hair-fix-3. Short all over and close to the shape of his skull, with no dome, helmet or volume on top; a little more length at the front, brushed slightly up and back; a thin, even layer of hair down each side to the top of his ears, which show just past it. Very dark brown-black with soft highlights on top: never flat black and never brown. A fine, smooth texture with no curls, coils, waves or bumpy outline. The same haircut in all 8 slots.
- RENDERING: smooth, soft, even shading on his face, skin and shirt, exactly like ref-4 and ref-current. No angular, faceted, patchy or painterly shading, and no extra wrinkles.
- PROPS: only the props the sheet names, each drawn the same in every slot that uses it: simple, solid, slightly toy-like, with clean shapes and bold colours, big enough to read when he is 100 pixels tall. Charts, boards and screens show plain shapes and colours only: no text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere, unless the sheet allows a single symbol. Props never hide his face.
```

## Hand back

Send each batch's sheets as one zip. Claude reviews them, adds them to the current source sheets and runs `python -I scripts/build-mascot-packs.py <folder> --keep-missing --preview <scratch>`, which matches skin, head size and thin side hair to the live sprite like every other sheet; then `python -I scripts/audit-mascot-heads.py --check`, and wires each tool's scenes (`src/lib/agent/mascot/context/tool-scenes.ts`).
